items.reason: Needs swift-w3c/swift-w3c-xml. W3C_XML.parse(_:maxDepth:) (Sources/W3C XML/W3C_XML.Parse.Document.swift) keeps its cursor in a local ArraySlice and throws W3C_XML.Parse.Error, whose cases carry no position, so swift-xml has nothing to read the offset from. Re-parsing with the token-based W3C_XML.Parser (whose __W3CXMLParserError does carry W3C_XML.Position) would be a second parser with different strictness and end-of-token positions, not the failing cursor. Recommended fix: in swift-w3c-xml, throw a located error (W3C_XML.Parse.Error plus W3C_XML.Position computed from the cursor's offset into the input, with line/column derived from it) from parse/fragment; then XML.Located/XML.Parse map it into XML.LocatedError(offset:) and XML.Error.syntax(line:column:), and add the multi-line / multibyte tests here.

notes: XML gained an internal @usableFromInline stored Bool `placeholder`; public init(_:) sets it false and the internal static `XML.null` sets it true; isNull reads the flag. Synthesized Hashable/== now also compare the flag (a placeholder no longer equals a real <_null/> element). The placeholder still serializes as <_null/> as before. XML.Located still reports offset 0 (issue #5).
